steps.expected: Section displays with the event as upcoming.

steps.action: Reload the Home Page.
steps.expected: Section still displays the same event unchanged, since it has not been manually unpinned.

title: Verify that an admin can pin a published event, enable Active Status, save, and see it appear on the Home Page after cache refresh

steps.expected: Event selected in the Event Selector.

steps.action: Set Active Status to enabled.

steps.action: Wait for cache refresh and load the Home Page.

title: Verify that confirming the passed-date warning proceeds to pin the event successfully
description: Admin acknowledges the warning and proceeds.

steps.action: Select a published event whose date has passed.
When the warning dialog appears, click the confirm/proceed option.
Click Save.
steps.expected: Configuration saves with success toast; the passed-date event is now the Pinned Event.

title: Verify that cancelling the passed-date warning aborts the pin action and retains the previous configuration
description: Admin declines the warning.

steps.action: Confirm Event A (a valid future-dated event) is the currently saved Pinned Event.
Select a passed-date event B instead.
When the warning dialog appears, click Cancel.
steps.expected: The pin action is aborted; the Pinned Event field reverts to/remains Event A; no configuration change is saved.

title: Verify that the Home Page shows the previously pinned event immediately after a Pin Configuration save, before cache refresh completes
description: Tests the stale-cache window between save and refresh.

steps.action: Confirm Event A is currently pinned and cached on the Home Page.
In Pin Configuration, pin Event B and save.
Immediately reload the Home Page before the cache refresh interval elapses.
steps.expected: Home Page may still show Event A (stale cache) without erroring.

steps.action: Reload again after the cache refresh interval elapses.
steps.expected: After refresh, Home Page shows Event B correctly.

title: Verify that a pinned event with a date equal to today is still treated as upcoming and displays normally
description: Boundary case - today is neither clearly upcoming nor passed.

steps.action: Pin a published event whose date is set to today's date.
Save the configuration.
steps.expected: Configuration saves successfully with no passed-date warning triggered.

steps.action: Load the Home Page.
steps.expected: The section displays the event normally as an upcoming event.

title: Verify that two admins saving different Pin Configurations in quick succession results in a single consistent final state
description: Concurrent-write scenario - confirms no duplicate/corrupted configuration record.

steps.action: Admin 1 opens Pin Configuration and selects Event A.
steps.expected: Admin 1's session shows Event A selected.

steps.action: Admin 2 opens Pin Configuration and selects Event B.
steps.expected: Admin 2's session shows Event B selected.

steps.action: Admin 1 saves, immediately followed by Admin 2 saving.
Reload the Pin Configuration screen.
steps.expected: The Pin Configuration reflects exactly one final state (the last successful save), with no duplicate or corrupted record.

title: Verify that unpinning an event while a visitor already has the Home Page open does not break their current page view
description: Confirms graceful behavior for an already-rendered page when the underlying configuration changes mid-session.

steps.action: Visitor loads the Home Page with an event pinned and visible.
Without the visitor refreshing, an admin unpins the event and saves.
steps.expected: Configuration is updated on the backend.

steps.action: Observe the visitor's already-open page (no manual refresh).
steps.expected: The visitor's open page continues to show the previously loaded event without erroring.

steps.action: Visitor manually refreshes the page.
steps.expected: After refresh, the section is no longer shown for the visitor.

title: Verify that a user lacking permission cannot bypass the Access Denied restriction via a direct configuration save request
description: Confirms the permission check is enforced server-side.

steps.action: Log in as a user without Home Page management permission.
Attempt to submit a Pin Configuration save action directly (bypassing the normal UI flow).
steps.expected: The save attempt is rejected with the bilingual Access Denied message.

steps.action: Check the Pin Configuration state afterward.
steps.expected: The Pin Configuration remains unchanged from before the attempt.

title: Verify that a visitor can view the pinned event details and navigate to its detail page by clicking the event image
description: A published event is pinned and active.

steps.action: Ensure a published event is pinned with Active Status enabled.
Load the Home Page and scroll to the Upcoming Event section.
steps.expected: Section renders in the two-column layout.

steps.action: Read the section tag, title, date, time, location, and short description.
steps.expected: All details display correctly and match the Events module record.

steps.action: Click the event image.
steps.expected: Browser navigates to the event's detail page.

title: Verify that the Upcoming Events section stops rendering when the pinned event is deleted entirely from the Events module
description: Distinguishes hard deletion from unpublishing.

steps.action: Pin a published event and confirm it displays on the Home Page.
Delete that event entirely from the Events module.
Wait for cache refresh.
Reload the Home Page.
steps.expected: The Upcoming Events section does not render; no broken/blank card or error is shown.

title: Verify that re-publishing a previously unpublished pinned event causes the section to reappear without re-pinning
description: Recovery scenario following TC-034.

steps.action: Pin a published event; unpublish it from the Events module and confirm the section disappears.
Re-publish the same event in the Events module without touching Pin Configuration.
Wait for cache refresh.
Reload the Home Page.
steps.expected: The Upcoming Events section reappears showing the same event automatically.
